correctness.rationale: The translated vertex orbits follow from Bayer et al., Thm. 2.3(b); the strictly increasing positive labels ensure no coincident ranks. For fixed ranks, opposite rearrangement minimizes the dot product. If their sum exceeds n, each endpoint's smallest positive label is on a shared coordinate in an opposite arrangement. Delete the smaller of the two minima: its partner is at least the larger minimum, so the squared distance strictly increases by u(2v-u). This excludes sums above n+1 from the second shell. For sums below n, one can add a new minimum in a vacant coordinate; for a fixed disjoint rank sum, strict discrete concavity of F gives balanced ranks and, at sum n, the next-best imbalance. At the diametral ranks, any defective pair has overlap cost at least 2t_m^2 in even dimension or 2t_mt_{m+1} in odd dimension, more than the missing-slot deficit t_m^2. For sum n+1 the minimum positive product requires just one overlap and both minima at that coordinate. Counting placements of the distinct labels gives n! at each winning rank/overlap pattern, with factor 1/2 exactly when one can exchange equal-rank endpoints. These arguments prove the second distinct level and all ties. Independent exact orbit-compressed enumeration (/workspace/replay/parking.py) reproduced both levels and each second-shell geometry/count in 132 label lists at n=4,5,6, including (D,D2,count)=(112692,102692,240) on the three-mechanism tie. Computations corroborate the all-parameter argument; the result is not for b_1=1, graph distances, or the continuous polytope.

value.rationale: The next distinct Euclidean chord length and its all-pair census refine the diameter of a standard polytope. The formula replaces enormous vertex-pair enumeration by a linear-size list; variable gaps change which geometry wins and can force ties.
